subject: Private deployment discovery — on-prem KMS & network constraints

Subject: Private deployment discovery — on-prem KMS & network constraints

Hi Matt / Sonia,

Thanks again for taking time earlier today. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the key pain points, your current environment, and agreed next steps so we have a single reference. Please correct anything I’ve misstated.

High-level pain points you described:
- Regulated PHI workloads: data must remain inside Aegis network and meet audit controls.
- No outbound egress for inference calls from air-gapped segments; some pockets allow limited, controlled outbound.
- Requirement to use customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) and strict key rotation policies.
- Need predictable latency and throughput for real-time chart summarization (p95 < 400ms).

Current stack (what you told us):
- On-prem Kubernetes cluster (RKE) with VLAN-isolated pods for PHI workloads.
- Central Vault (HashiCorp) with HSM-backed keywrap; KMS endpoints are internal-only.
- Existing inference experiments on a private GPU pool; model artifacts stored on an internal OCI registry.

Success criteria for an initial pilot:
1) Private/VPC deployment inside Aegis network (no model tokens or inference traffic leaving the VPC from PHI zone).
2) Integration with your Vault/HSM for key management; Redwood cannot hold unwrapped customer keys.
3) Pass of basic security checks: network isolation verification, audit log forwarding, and SOC2 evidence review.
4) Demonstrate steady-state latency under load with our Dedicated runtime in your environment.

Constraints/unknowns we flagged that need follow-up:
- Which subnets allow controlled outbound egress (for model updates/telemetry)?
- Whether the OCI registry supports our signed-image verification process.
- Exact HSM vendor & interface (PKCS#11, KMIP, cloud-HSM?).

Agreed next steps:
- Aegis to share a short network diagram and list of allowed egress CIDRs (attaching template: aegis_network_outline.pdf).
- Redwood SE (Priyom) to run a short technical questionnaire and propose a minimal on-prem architecture diagram.
- Exchange of SOC2 extract and SOC2 scope discussion (we received soc2-extract-2025.pdf).
- Schedule a 90-minute architecture workshop (SE + Infra + Security) — target next week.

I’ve attached the quick template for the network diagram and dropped a copy of our on-prem guide ahead of the workshop.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate calendars once you confirm a few windows.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Vanessa,

Thanks for the clear summary — looks accurate. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Most PHI traffic lives in an air-gapped VLAN; we cannot run inference calls out of that VLAN. We do maintain a small "staging egress" subnet used for pulls/updates which is tightly firewalled and requires firewall rules change requests for any new destination.
- Our HSM vendor is Thales (nShield) and the keywrap interface is PKCS#11. Keys are never exportable in plaintext.
- For the pilot we'll need a plan that avoids any persistent telemetry that captures PHI outside the VPC; auditing logs forwarded for SRE purposes must be scrubbed of identifiable fields.

On attachments: I uploaded a rough network sketch to the Drive link you listed and attached a sanitized SOC2 extract (already in the thread).

Next: Sonia (cc’d) will propose two time windows for the architecture workshop — Wednesday 5/19 or Friday 5/21, mornings PT.

-Matt

Hi Matt / Vanessa,

Appreciate the detail — a few technical notes and questions ahead of the architecture workshop. I’ll bring these to the call but wanted to capture them so your infra team can prepare.

Technical questions / assumptions:
1) HSM integration: PKCS#11 support is straightforward; we’ll need service account mapping and a short test harness to validate sign/unseal operations. Can you confirm whether the HSM is reachable from the Kubernetes control plane namespace?
2) Image distribution: Redwood can support a signed-image workflow. Does your OCI registry support OCI distribution spec and bearer-token auth? If not, we can propose a pull-proxy pattern that runs in a non-PHI subnet to cache images.
3) Telemetry & logs: Redwood’s private deployment supports full control of telemetry endpoints. For the pilot we will disable application-level telemetry by default and rely on host-level metrics that you can forward to your ELK.
4) Air-gap mode: We’ve run air-gapped installs before (requires pre-staging model artifacts and an offline installer). That will add ~2–3 days to the initial setup for the pilot.

Proposed artifacts I’ll bring to the workshop:
- Minimal on-prem architecture diagram (attachment: redwood_onprem_guide.pdf)
- A short runbook for HSM test harness & verification steps
- Pre-flight checklist for network ACLs / firewall rules

If you can confirm PKCS#11 endpoint accessibility and whether the OCI registry supports token auth before the call, we can tailor the runbook.

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.

Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

Thanks — PKCS#11 endpoint is reachable from the control plane; I’ll have infra bring the exact socket path and a quick onboarding note for the workshop.

OCI registry: supports bearer token auth and the distribution spec. We should be fine with signed images.

Sonia and I confirmed 5/19 09:00–10:30 PT works for the workshop. I’ll send a calendar invite to the group and share a brief internal runbook for firewall request process.

Also, one ask: can Redwood provide a short statement describing your private deployment data flow and guarantees (no PHI egress, keys never leave HSM) that we can share with our compliance team ahead of the workshop? If you can email that over, we’ll fast-track the internal approval.

-Matt
